s2289: According to paragraph 2 of Article 36 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, an intersection where the order of movement is determined by the signals of a traffic light or a traffic officer is a controlled intersection. If a flashing yellow light is on, or there is no traffic light or it is not working, or there is no traffic officer, the intersection is considered uncontrolled, and the driver must follow the rules for passing through uncontrolled intersections and the priority signs installed at the intersection. According to subparagraphs "c" and "d" of paragraph 4 of the same Article, at an uncontrolled intersection: c) at an intersection of roads of equal importance, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right; drivers of rail vehicles must follow the same rule among themselves; at such an intersection a rail vehicle has priority over a trackless vehicle, regardless of its direction of travel; d) when turning left or making a U-turn, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction on a road of equal importance that are going straight ahead or turning right. Drivers of rail vehicles must follow the same rule among themselves.
